## Existing owners, not a second planner

The existing .github/test-proof-plan.yaml owns executable selection. Its seven
whole-root selectors implement B's finite assignment. The admission complement
continues to select non-debt roots (and all testpostgres); its 17 retained debt
roots and the six finite debt selectors are explicit. A future unassigned debt
root refuses canonical BindExecution rather than silently disappearing.

The pre-partition persistenceDebtAdmissionRun is retained ONLY for exact
before/after comparison. The existing planner binds both plans against the same
current discovery and parity/catalog evidence. Controls compare every bound
RequiredTest including children/backends and count, environment, workload,
timeout and budget, plus complete package sets and unrelated deferrals, in all
six venue/tier combinations. The dedicated census ProofUnit compares unchanged.
Current source conservation is 355 roots: 229 admission + 124 PG + 2 census.

New controls cover omitted/duplicate/reassigned roots, foreign selection,
partial backend/case filters, skip, timeout, cache policy, budget, environment,
package/testpostgres loss, packing, narrowed child obligations, an eighth unit,
missing profile membership and duplicate membership. Existing source-partition
validation checks actual store and PG declarations. Native go test -run calls
on a finite synthetic 229-root fixture prove exactly all roots AND both complete
backend/case descendants (1145 PASS identities), without selecting a leaf.
This is selector-mechanics proof, not execution of the 229 business proofs.

Timing inventory checks every new unit at ordinary 240/312 boundaries, including
overrun refusal, while preserving census 600/780 exactly. Changed selections
cannot reuse the old 183s weight or the mixed planning estimates; the existing
unknown-weight fallback applies until the real publisher has complete evidence.
The spec's retained-controls pointer now enumerates all seven existing owners;
the execution census owner/tiers/rule are unchanged. Catalog/plan consumers run
through their existing inventories; no alternate registry or planner was added.
